/**
 * Mark a server-dispatched Behavior run completed, recording who executed it.
 *
 * `complete_window` defaults `runs.model_used` to the literal 'external-client'
 * whenever its caller omits `model` (see complete-window.ts), and the platform's
 * own Lobu agent omits it — so a run the SERVER dispatched ends up labelled as
 * though an outside MCP client had executed it. That label reads as an
 * observation and is not one: triaging the July 2026 Behavior collapse from this
 * column produced exactly that wrong conclusion.
 *
 * This path is reached only for runs the server dispatched to the Lobu agent —
 * it is keyed on `dispatched_message_id`, which only `watchers/automation.ts`
 * sets — so the executor is known here. Mirrors the device-worker stamp in
 * `worker-api/run-lifecycle.ts`. A model the agent DID report always wins; this
 * only replaces the placeholder.
 *
 * (SQL comments are kept out of the template literal: a backtick inside one
 * terminates the string and fails the esbuild transform, not just at runtime.)
 */
export async function markWatcherRunCompleted(
	sql: DbClient,
	runId: number,
	windowId: number | null
): Promise<void> {
	await sql`
    UPDATE runs
    SET status = 'completed',
        window_id = ${windowId},
        completed_at = current_timestamp,
        error_message = NULL,
        model_used = CASE
          WHEN model_used = 'external-client' OR model_used IS NULL
            THEN 'lobu-agent'
          ELSE model_used
        END
    WHERE id = ${runId}
      AND status = ANY(${runStatusLiteral(ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES)}::text[])
  `;
}

in the collapse itself; the retry storm around it IS one.

Prod DB is reachable directly: the `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` is the prod DB
(`summaries-db.brill-kanyu.ts.net:5432/owletto`). The `runs` table is NOT in the
`query_sql` allowlist — use `psql "$DATABASE_URL"`.

## Shape of the collapse

| day | completed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| Jul 25 | 17 | 0 |
| Jul 26 | 16 | 27 |
| Jul 27–28 | **0** | 288 / 979 |
| Jul 29 | 5 | 1113 |
| Jul 30 | 9 | 0 (after 19:16 Jul 29) |

~2,600 failed runs over four days against a ~16/day baseline. Blast radius is NARROW —
`count(DISTINCT watcher_id) = 2`, `count(DISTINCT organization_id) = 1`. Two Behaviors
hard-failing at full retry rate, not a fleet outage.

## ISSUE #2350 — the two gaps, second is sharper

1. **No failover when an inference provider is exhausted.** One provider's quota takes
   its Behaviors to zero.
2. **A terminal provider error is retried as if transient.** The 429 names its own reset
   time (`2026-07-31`) and was retried ~2,000 times anyway. Burns scheduler/worker
   capacity on work that cannot succeed, floods `runs` with ~1,000 identical rows/day
   (which is what hid it), and will hammer the provider the moment quota returns.
   A 429 carrying a reset timestamp should park the Behavior until that time, or trip a
   per-provider+org circuit breaker.

**Fix (2) before (1)** — honouring the reset stops the bleeding immediately and costs far
less than a failover design, which needs a decision about which provider a workspace falls
back to and who pays.

## RESOLVED: what actually ended the collapse at ~19:15 UTC Jul 29

Two independent causes had to clear, and they cleared 40 minutes apart:

1. **~18:35 UTC** — the provider switch to Gemini stopped the z.ai 429s.
2. **~19:15 UTC** — **#2319** (`b8e66f02`, "deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model",
   merged 17:12 UTC) finished rolling out. Before it, the agent never received the MCP
   instructions telling it to call `completeWindow`, so runs reached the provider fine and
   then failed at the finalize step.

The data separates them cleanly: `completeWindow` failures number **404 before** the #2319
merge and **14 after**, with the **last one at 19:14:00**. Since 19:16 every Behavior run has
completed — 9/9, zero failures. Jul 30 has zero `completeWindow` failures at all.

So both changes were load-bearing; neither alone would have recovered Behaviors. The
"completeWindow is a separate unfixed bug" worry is CLOSED — #2319 fixed it.

## Third failure class — now closed (kept for the history)

`Agent reply finished without calling run_sdk (client.behaviors.completeWindow)` — 367 over
four days, spanning Jul 20 → Jul 29, independent of the quota. It OUTLIVED it: z.ai's last
429 was 18:35 Jul 29, and the final platform-inference runs (19:09–19:14) all failed this
way instead. Plus 55 `agent didn't finish responding in time`. Never fixed. Worth re-testing
now that [[project_system_prompt_override_is_inert]] (#2319) is deployed.

## Gemini is configured and VERIFIED (2026-07-30)

- `inference_providers`: `gemini` is `is_default=t`, active, `capabilities` =
  `{"text":{"model":"gemini-2.5-pro"}}` (the field [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]

- `agents.models` for personal-agent lists `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` first.
- The `.env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` is valid — direct `gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent` → 200.
- **End-to-end proof:** `client.conversations.send({agent_id:'personal-finance',
  thread:'zz-gemini-probe', text:'Reply with exactly: GEMINI OK'})` returned `"GEMINI OK"`
  in 5.6s, and the run row showed `claimed_by='gateway-…'` with `model_used` empty

## Behaviors DO run on the platform (corrected 2026-07-30)

An earlier pass in this same session concluded "an external MCP client claims every
Behavior run, so Gemini never serves one." **That was wrong.** Two labels misled me:

- `claimed_by = 'lobu:personal-agent'` is stamped by the platform's OWN dispatcher,
  `packages/server/src/watchers/automation.ts:1362`, right before it posts the dispatch
  message to an embedded Lobu agent session (`thread: watcher-<runId>`, `forceNew`,
  `intent.kind='behavior_run'` — the same path #2342 isolates). The `lobu:` prefix means
  "handed to the Lobu agent", not "an outside client took it".
- `model_used = 'external-client'` is a DEFAULT, not an observation:
  `tools/admin/manage_behaviors/complete-window.ts:67` uses it whenever `complete_window`
  is called without a `model` arg, which the Lobu agent does.

Ground truth is in `run_metadata`: `{"executor":"lobu-agent","agent_id":"personal-agent",
"session_agent_id":"personal-agent_watcher_5_run_802958","dispatch_source":"scheduled"}`.

So Behaviors run through the platform on the agent's configured provider (Gemini), and the
Jul 29 19:16 recovery IS consistent with the provider switch. There is no rogue process and
nothing to disconnect.

**Real gap this exposed:** the `runs` table cannot tell you which model or provider served a
Behavior — the column that looks like it does is defaulted to a constant. Any triage that
reasons from `model_used` will be wrong. Read `run_metadata.executor` instead.

"the Gemini switch fixed it"; (3) reading `model_used='external-client'` + `claimed_by='lobu:…'`

thing — `error_message` grouped, then `claimed_by`, then finally the CODE that writes those
columns. The lesson that actually generalizes: **a status column is only evidence if you have
read the line that writes it.** Both columns here are defaults/prefixes chosen by the
platform, and both read like something else. See [[feedback_judge_reviews_by_findings_not_scores]].

---
name: reference_worktree_remove_fails_with_submodules
description: "git worktree remove refuses on every lobu worktree (owletto submodule) — use rm -rf + git worktree prune; budget ~20s each because of node_modules"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/<name>` fails on **every** lobu worktree with:

```
fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed
```

That is the `owletto` submodule, which `make task-setup` pins into each worktree — so it
is not an occasional case, it is all of them.

Working removal:

```sh
rm -rf ".claude/worktrees/<name>" && git worktree prune
```

`git worktree prune` (from the main checkout) reaps the stale metadata afterwards. This
does NOT delete the branch ref — commits stay reachable via `refs/heads/<branch>`, which
is what makes a bulk sweep low-risk even if one entry is misclassified.

**Budget the time.** Each worktree carries a populated `node_modules`, so `rm -rf` runs
~15–25s. A 31-worktree sweep exceeded a 10-minute foreground timeout at 22 removed —
run bulk cleanup in the background.

## Picking what is safe to remove

Do NOT classify by ancestry. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` reports `1` for
almost every squash-merged branch, because a squash writes a new commit with no ancestry
link (see [[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]]). On a 67-worktree sweep that
misread 29 merged branches as unmerged.

Classify against real PR state instead:

```sh
gh pr list --state merged --limit 400 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/merged.txt
gh pr list --state open   --limit 200 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/open.txt
```

Remove only when the tree is clean AND the branch is in the merged list. Re-check
`git status --porcelain` immediately before each `rm -rf` rather than trusting an earlier
snapshot — worktrees go dirty on their own from build artifacts (`pi-loader-hardening`
did exactly that mid-sweep and was correctly skipped).

Answering the "do we have it already" part first, since it changes whether the rest is even worth discussing.

**We don't have failover. Nothing in the repo retries against a different provider or model** — I had a read-only agent trace the whole path and it found no partial or disabled implementation to switch on.

What we *do* have is easy to mistake for it:

- `agents.models` is an ordered list, and two places genuinely walk past `[0]` — `message-handler-bridge.ts:208` and `provider-catalog.ts:497`. But both run **before dispatch** and key on *"does this provider have credentials and route?"*, never on an error.
- There's a credential tier chain (user profile → org key → system env) at `secret-proxy.ts:294`. It fires only when a tier returns *nothing*. A 429 on the org's key never reaches the system key.
- At run time the model is resolved once (`session-runner.ts:785`) and the proxy is pure passthrough — `secret-proxy.ts:1032` logs a non-ok upstream and relays it verbatim.

The only 429 retry is inside vendored `pi-coding-agent`: blind exponential backoff, same session, same model, 3 attempts. It ignores `Retry-After`. So does everything else — there is no `Retry-After`/`x-ratelimit-reset` parsing anywhere on the inference path.

content.text:
Correction to what I told you earlier, since it changes this decision: I said #2335 fixed #2350's retry storm and closed it. That was overstated. `advanceScheduleAfterTerminalFailure` advances `next_run_at` to the next cron tick on terminal failure, which does kill the tight re-claim loop that produced ~2000 rows. But it never classifies the 429 — a Behavior on an exhausted provider still burns one failed run *every tick* until quota returns. The storm is bounded, not the waste.

## Why you'd want failover

The real argument isn't the outage size — blast radius was 2 Behaviors in 1 org. It's that **Behaviors are unattended**. A chat user sees "provider quota exhausted" and switches provider in 30 seconds. A scheduled Behavior at 3am has nobody to do that, so a provider quota becomes a silent multi-day outage. That's what happened: Jul 27–28 had *zero* completions and nothing surfaced it.

## Why I'd not build it yet

Three things make it a bigger decision than it looks:

- **Whose budget.** Falling back to the platform system key means Lobu pays for a customer's exhausted quota. That's a pricing decision, not an engineering one.
- **Consent.** Silently routing a workspace's prompts to a different vendor is a data-residency problem. Some customers will consider that worse than the outage.
- **It wasn't the fix.** The collapse ended because you switched to Gemini — config, not code. Failover would have masked an exhausted free tier rather than surfacing it.

## What I'd do instead

The cheaper 80% is to make exhaustion *terminal and visible*: park the Behavior until the 429's reset timestamp instead of retrying it every tick, and surface a "provider exhausted" state. That converts a silent two-day outage into an obvious one, and it's strictly a prerequisite for failover anyway — you can't fail over from a condition you don't detect. Right now nothing parses `Retry-After` on the inference path at all.

And if you *do* want failover later, the seam already exists — which is the useful finding here. `models[]` is already an ordered list, and `message-handler-bridge.ts:208` already walks it at dispatch time skipping providers that aren't routable. So failover is: write a per-`(org, provider)` cooldown row when a 429 names a reset, and make `providerIsRoutable()` consult it. The existing walk then does the failover for free — no runtime retry-and-reroute, no second retry budget, no new coordination. That fits the "put the check at the chokepoint" rule rather than bolting on a parallel mechanism.

So my recommendation: **don't build failover; build the detection**. It's smaller, it's a prerequisite, and it gives you the data to decide whether failover is even warranted beyond one org.

That's your call though — it's a product question, not a technical one.

`next_run_at` to the next cron tick on terminal failure — that kills the tight re-claim
loop that produced ~2,000 rows. It does NOT classify the 429: a Behavior on an exhausted
provider still burns one failed run **every tick** until quota returns. Nothing anywhere
parses `Retry-After` / `x-ratelimit-reset` on the inference path.

**Gap 1 (failover) — CONFIRMED ABSENT, and the seam for it already exists.** Full
read-only trace found no runtime provider/model failover: model is resolved once per
session (`agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts:785`), the gateway proxy is pure
passthrough on a non-ok upstream (`gateway/proxy/secret-proxy.ts:1032`), the only 429
retry is vendored pi-coding-agent's blind same-model backoff, and the queue's
`scheduleRetry` never inspects the error. `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` exists but its ONLY
consumer is a UI CTA (`core/src/errors.ts:251`) — no scheduler/router branches on it.

Things that LOOK like failover and are not: `agents.models` past `[0]` is walked only
pre-dispatch and only for credential/routability
(`gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:208`,
`gateway/auth/provider-catalog.ts:497`); the credential tier chain
(user profile → org key → system env, `secret-proxy.ts:294`) fires on credential
ABSENCE only, so a 429 on the org key never reaches the system key.

**Design if failover is ever wanted:** do NOT add runtime retry-and-reroute. Write a
per-`(org, provider)` cooldown row when a 429 names a reset, and make
`providerIsRoutable()` consult it — the EXISTING pre-dispatch walk then fails over for
free. No second retry budget, no new coordination. Blocked on a product call regardless:
whose budget pays for a customer's exhausted quota, and whether silently rerouting a
workspace's prompts to another vendor is acceptable (data residency).
